name: Username enumeration
description:
The application answers a failed login differently depending on whether the submitted username exists. With the same wrong password, a known username and several invented ones produced responses that differ consistently - in status code, in message or in page structure - while each side was stable across repeats. An attacker can use the difference to compile a list of valid accounts, which makes password guessing, credential stuffing and targeted phishing much more efficient.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no username-enumeration entry. It is classified under CWE-204 (observable response discrepancy).
remediation: Return the same response for every failed authentication, whatever the reason: the same status code, the same message (for example "Invalid username or password"), the same page structure and, as far as practical, the same response time - including running the password hash comparison for accounts that do not exist. Apply the same rule to registration, password-reset and account-recovery flows, which leak account existence in the same way.
